# mission-facts.js
n9wlfwz Apollo 11 landed on the Moon on July 20, 1969. The descent stage stayed on the Moon; the ascent stage lifted off with Armstrong and Aldrin. The complete model does not show what was left intact at the site.
tm8larc Spirit got stuck in soft ground in 2009. Its last communication was on March 22, 2010, and NASA closed the mission in 2011. It was struggling to get enough power and survive the Martian winter.
i6s4kpk A planet-wide dust storm in 2018 cut the light reaching Opportunity's panels. The last communication was on June 10, 2018. After the recovery attempts, NASA declared the mission over in 2019.
nzy55dr Dust piling up on the solar panels reduced InSight's power. The last communication was on December 15, 2022, and NASA declared the mission over that month. SEIS studied marsquakes.
0xjzmmn Phoenix studied ice and soil in the Martian Arctic. Its last communication was on November 2, 2008. Winter cut the sunlight and worsened the thermal conditions of the lander.
3vnfkp3 Viking 1 used radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs), not solar panels. Its surface module stopped working on November 11, 1982, after a faulty command.
hs0uwn1 The Viking 2 surface module used RTGs and stopped transmitting in April 1980. Viking 1 and Viking 2 landed in different places: Chryse Planitia and Utopia Planitia.
n0m4thy Sojourner was NASA's first rover on Mars. It arrived with Mars Pathfinder on July 4, 1997. It analyzed rocks with the APXS and communicated through the landing module. Pathfinder's last contact was on September 27, 1997.
t6361ms Surveyor 3 stayed in Oceanus Procellarum. Apollo 12 visited the probe in 1969 and recovered several parts, including the camera and the scoop, to study how the lunar environment had affected them.
ymm8fsz Mariner 9 was the first spacecraft to orbit another planet. The mission ended on October 27, 1972. This archive has no current location or confirmed impact; a historic orbital prediction does not confirm its fate.
ze7ks8d Lunar Orbiter 1 photographed possible Apollo sites. NASA steered the spacecraft into an impact on the Moon on October 29, 1966. The viewer shows the historic spacecraft, not intact remains at the impact site.
o6en430 The Deep Space 2 microprobes Scott and Amundsen were meant to pierce the ground near the Martian south pole. No signal was received after the planned arrival on December 3, 1999. The exact site is unknown and the cause of the loss is not confirmed.
mesvenj The Apollo 15 LRV was the first vehicle driven by astronauts on the Moon. It ran on batteries and had four wheels; it stayed on the surface when the exploration ended.
zdzvkse The Apollo 16 LRV made it possible to explore the Descartes highlands. The battery-powered, four-wheeled rover stayed on the lunar surface.
umd3o76 The Apollo 17 LRV was used at Taurus–Littrow. Its wire-mesh wheels and batteries carried the astronauts around; the vehicle stayed on the Moon.
